main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the advanced English language skills
specific_competence_name: Automate the production of oral descriptions and conversations using standard pronunciation (e.g., phonemes, syllables, stress and intonation)
learning_activity_name: Articulate sentences in connected speech with standard pronunciation (e.g., phonemes, syllables, stress and intonation)
sla_name: Connected speech and standard pronunciation
sla_assessment_criteria: Words and sentences are articulated with appropriate pronunciation in connected speech.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Connected speech is the natural flow of spoken English in which sounds, syllables and words influence one another. Standard pronunciation follows the accepted model of the language.
sla_notes_details: Learners study phonemes (vowels, consonants, diphthongs), syllable division, word stress, sentence stress and intonation (rising, falling and fall-rise). In connected speech, features such as linking (go on), assimilation (ten pounds sounds like tem pounds), elision (next day sounds like nex day) and weak forms (to, for, and) appear. Learners transcribe short sentences, mark stress and practise reading them aloud with a natural rhythm.
sla_notes_illustrations: In the sentence: I want to go to the market, the content words want, go and market are stressed, while to is reduced to a weak form /tə/. A falling tone at the end signals a statement, and a rising tone in Are you coming? signals a yes/no question.
sla_notes_daily_life: Clear pronunciation and correct stress help students in interviews, presentations, phone calls and when speaking with foreigners, tourists and colleagues.
sla_exercise: What is a phoneme?::The smallest unit of sound that can change the meaning of a word.||Which words are normally stressed in a sentence?::Content words such as nouns, main verbs, adjectives and adverbs.||Name the intonation pattern used for a yes/no question.::Rising intonation.||What is elision?::The omission of a sound in fast speech, as in nex day for next day.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the advanced English language skills
specific_competence_name: Automate the production of oral descriptions and conversations using standard pronunciation (e.g., phonemes, syllables, stress and intonation)
learning_activity_name: Describe objects, events and situations with appropriate English expressions (e.g., level of formality, pre-supposition, time, audience and topics)
sla_name: Describing objects, events and situations orally
sla_assessment_criteria: Objects, events and situation are described in English with appropriate levels of formality, presupposition, time, audience and topics.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Oral description means presenting the features of an object, event or situation to listeners using suitable expressions.
sla_notes_details: A good description considers the audience, topic, level of formality and time. Learners use descriptive adjectives, prepositions of place, sequencing words (first, then, finally), tense choice (past for events already finished, present for general facts) and presuppositions, which are things assumed to be known by the listener. Formal contexts need polite and precise language while informal contexts allow contractions and idioms.
sla_notes_illustrations: To describe a school assembly to a visitor, a student may say: Every Monday at seven thirty, all students gather on the parade ground; the head prefect leads the national anthem, then the teacher on duty gives announcements.
sla_notes_daily_life: Describing skills are used when giving directions, reporting an accident to the police, describing a lost item or presenting a product to customers.
sla_exercise: Name two factors that determine the register in an oral description.::The audience and the level of formality (or topic and time).||What is a presupposition?::Information that the speaker assumes the listener already knows.||Which tense is normally used to describe a completed event?::The simple past tense.||Give two sequencing words used in describing an event.::First and finally (or then, next).

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the advanced English language skills
specific_competence_name: Automate the production of oral descriptions and conversations using standard pronunciation (e.g., phonemes, syllables, stress and intonation)
learning_activity_name: Participate in discussions on various topical issues (e.g., entrepreneurship, corruption, taxation, child right and security, gender education, cyber security education, disaster management, health and productive education, drug abuse, life skills, financial management education and taxation) with a standard pronunciation
sla_name: Participating in discussions on topical issues
sla_assessment_criteria: Topical issues are logically discussed.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A discussion is an organised exchange of ideas among people on a topic of common interest.
sla_notes_details: Learners discuss issues such as entrepreneurship, corruption, taxation, child rights, security and gender education. They use skills of opening a point, agreeing, disagreeing politely, asking for clarification, interrupting appropriately, giving evidence and summarising. Group work roles include chairperson, secretary and contributors. Speakers avoid personal attacks and respect turn-taking.
sla_notes_illustrations: In a group discussing corruption, one student says: I agree that corruption slows development; however, I think weak enforcement of laws is also a key cause. Another asks: Could you give an example to support that?
sla_notes_daily_life: Discussion skills are used in staff meetings, village assemblies, school clubs, parliamentary debates and community radio programmes.
sla_exercise: Give two expressions for disagreeing politely.::I see your point, but... and I am afraid I do not agree.||What is the role of a chairperson in a discussion?::To guide the discussion, give turns and keep to the topic.||Why should speakers avoid personal attacks?::Because a discussion should address ideas, not people.||Name two topical issues that can be discussed.::Corruption and taxation (or entrepreneurship, gender education).

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the advanced English language skills
specific_competence_name: Develop vocabulary from conversations and written texts
learning_activity_name: Write unfamiliar vocabulary from given complex oral and written texts
sla_name: Identifying and writing unfamiliar vocabulary from texts
sla_assessment_criteria: Unfamiliar vocabulary from given texts are written correctly.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Unfamiliar vocabulary consists of words a learner meets in oral or written texts and cannot yet understand or use.
sla_notes_details: While listening or reading, learners note down new words, record the sentence in which each appears, its part of speech, a pronunciation guide and a tentative meaning. They keep a vocabulary notebook or digital glossary, organised by topic or alphabet. Complex texts such as academic articles, speeches and reports provide many technical and abstract words such as ambiguity, paradigm and sustainability.
sla_notes_illustrations: From a lecture on the economy a student records: inflation (noun) - a general rise in prices - Inflation reduces the buying power of money.
sla_notes_daily_life: Building a personal word bank helps students prepare for examinations, read newspapers and follow news broadcasts with confidence.
sla_exercise: What details should be recorded for a new word?::Its spelling, part of speech, meaning and an example sentence.||Why is it useful to record the sentence where the word appeared?::It shows the context that helps to understand and remember the meaning.||Name one kind of text that provides advanced vocabulary.::An academic article, report or speech.||What is the part of speech of the word sustainability?::A noun.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the advanced English language skills
specific_competence_name: Develop vocabulary from conversations and written texts
learning_activity_name: Discover the meanings of vocabulary using context, technical dictionary, thesaurus and encyclopaedia
sla_name: Discovering meanings of vocabulary using reference sources
sla_assessment_criteria: Meanings of new vocabulary are discovered.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners discover the meaning of unknown words by using context clues and reference materials.
sla_notes_details: Context clues include definitions, synonyms, antonyms, examples and general sense. Reference tools include a general dictionary, a technical or subject dictionary (law, medicine, economics), a thesaurus that lists words of similar meaning, and an encyclopaedia that gives background information on people, places and concepts. Learners compare several sources and choose the meaning that fits the context.
sla_notes_illustrations: In the sentence: The witness was reluctant, hesitating before answering each question, the phrase hesitating before answering suggests that reluctant means unwilling.
sla_notes_daily_life: Using dictionaries and online references helps students to understand contracts, medical instructions and technical manuals.
sla_exercise: What is a thesaurus used for?::To find synonyms and antonyms of words.||Name two kinds of context clues.::Synonyms and examples (or definitions, antonyms).||Which source would give detailed background on a historical figure?::An encyclopaedia.||Why should one check a word in more than one source?::Because words can have different meanings depending on the context.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the advanced English language skills
specific_competence_name: Develop vocabulary from conversations and written texts
learning_activity_name: Form new words through word formation processes (e.g., compounding, blending, clipping)
sla_name: Word formation processes
sla_assessment_criteria: New words are formed correctly through different word formation process.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Word formation is the way new words are created in English.
sla_notes_details: Main processes include compounding (joining two words: blackboard), blending (parts of two words: brunch from breakfast and lunch; smog from smoke and fog), clipping (shortening: exam from examination), affixation (prefixes and suffixes: unhappiness), conversion (change of word class without change of form: to email from email), acronyms (NATO, HIV) and back-formation (edit from editor). Learners identify and create examples and use them in sentences.
sla_notes_illustrations: The word Bongo Flava is a blend of a place-based name and a music genre; the word motel is a blend of motor and hotel; the word phone is a clipping of telephone.
sla_notes_daily_life: Understanding word formation helps students to decode new words in media, technology and advertising, for example, cyberspace, podcast and edutainment.
sla_exercise: What is a blend? Give one example.::A word made from parts of two words, e.g. brunch.||Identify the word formation process in the word exam.::Clipping.||Which process forms the word blackboard?::Compounding.||What process forms NATO?::Acronym formation.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the advanced English language skills
specific_competence_name: Use correct grammar and vocabulary in oral and written language tasks
learning_activity_name: Use the synonyms and antonyms of given words to compose a variety of texts
sla_name: Using synonyms and antonyms in texts
sla_assessment_criteria: Synonyms and antonyms of given words are used properly in oral and written tasks.
sla_teaching_aids: Newspapers|Articles related to environment|Gender|Drug abuse|HIV|Road safety|Human rights
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Synonyms are words with similar meanings while antonyms are words with opposite meanings.
sla_notes_details: Learners study degrees of meaning, since synonyms are rarely identical (for example, thin, slim and skinny differ in tone). They study collocations, connotation and register and choose words that suit the context. Antonyms may be gradable (hot and cold), complementary (alive and dead) or relational (buy and sell). Learners compose paragraphs, descriptions and short stories using varied word choices to avoid repetition.
sla_notes_illustrations: Instead of repeating big in the sentence: The big company made big profits, a writer may say: The large company made substantial profits.
sla_notes_daily_life: Using synonyms makes reports, letters and speeches more interesting and precise while antonyms are useful in comparing and contrasting ideas.
sla_exercise: Give a synonym of the word difficult.::Hard, challenging or tough.||What kind of antonyms are buy and sell?::Relational antonyms.||Why are synonyms rarely identical in meaning?::They differ in tone, formality or connotation.||Give an antonym of generous.::Mean or stingy.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the advanced English language skills
specific_competence_name: Use correct grammar and vocabulary in oral and written language tasks
learning_activity_name: Use advanced vocabulary and grammar (e.g., tenses and subject-verb agreement) to describe events, objects and situations
sla_name: Using advanced vocabulary and grammar to describe events, objects and situations
sla_assessment_criteria: Events, objects and situations are described clearly using advanced grammar and vocabulary.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Advanced grammar and vocabulary allow speakers and writers to describe events, objects and situations accurately.
sla_notes_details: Learners review tenses (simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous) and their uses, and the rules of subject-verb agreement: singular subjects take singular verbs, collective nouns depend on the intended meaning, subjects joined by and are plural, and with either...or the verb agrees with the nearer subject. They also use complex sentences, relative clauses and precise adjectives and adverbs.
sla_notes_illustrations: Neither the manager nor the employees were aware of the change (verb agrees with the nearer subject, employees). By the time the police arrived, the thieves had escaped (past perfect shows the earlier action).
sla_notes_daily_life: Accurate grammar is expected in job applications, reports, interviews and formal presentations.
sla_exercise: Correct the sentence: The team are winning the cup.::The team is winning the cup (or are, if members are regarded as individuals).||Which tense is used for an action completed before another past action?::The past perfect tense.||Choose the correct verb: Either the teacher or the students (is/are) absent.::Are.||What is a relative clause? Give an example.::A clause that gives more information about a noun, e.g. the book that I bought.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the advanced English language skills
specific_competence_name: Use correct grammar and vocabulary in oral and written language tasks
learning_activity_name: Prepare and deliver complex speeches on various topics including cross-cutting issues using appropriate vocabulary and grammar (e.g., tenses and cohesive devices)
sla_name: Preparing and delivering complex speeches
sla_method: TIPS, Group discussion and Library search
sla_assessment_criteria: Complex speeches on various topics are well prepared and delivered using appropriate grammar and vocabulary.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A speech is a formal oral presentation given to an audience for a purpose such as informing, persuading or entertaining.
sla_notes_details: Steps include analysing the audience and purpose, researching the topic, outlining (introduction, body, conclusion), writing or preparing notes, rehearsing and delivering. Speakers use cohesive devices (firstly, moreover, in conclusion), correct tenses, rhetorical devices, eye contact, voice modulation and gestures. Cross-cutting issues such as environmental conservation, gender equality, HIV/AIDS and digital safety may be addressed.
sla_notes_illustrations: A speech on environmental conservation may open with a striking statistic, present three main arguments with examples, and conclude with a call to action: Let us plant a tree today for the generations of tomorrow.
sla_notes_daily_life: Speech skills are needed for graduation ceremonies, political campaigns, community meetings and business presentations.
sla_exercise: Name the three main parts of a speech.::Introduction, body and conclusion.||Give two cohesive devices used in a speech.::Moreover and in conclusion (or firstly, however).||Why is it important to analyse the audience?::To choose suitable content, language and tone.||Name one non-verbal skill for a speaker.::Eye contact (or gestures, posture, voice control).

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the advanced English language skills
specific_competence_name: Use correct grammar and vocabulary in oral and written language tasks
learning_activity_name: Write articles (e.g., newspaper articles, magazine articles and journal articles) about events, objects and situations using advanced vocabulary and grammar
sla_name: Writing articles for newspapers, magazines and journals
sla_assessment_criteria: Articles about events, objects and situations are written correctly using advanced vocabulary and grammar.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: An article is a written piece of non-fiction that informs, explains or argues about a topic for publication.
sla_notes_details: Learners study the features of newspaper articles (headline, byline, lead paragraph, body with the most important facts first), magazine articles (feature style, subheadings, engaging tone) and journal articles (abstract, introduction, methods, discussion, conclusion and references, in formal academic language). They plan, draft, edit and proofread, using advanced vocabulary and correct grammar and avoiding bias.
sla_notes_illustrations: A newspaper headline such as: Students Win National Science Fair is followed by a lead paragraph answering who, what, where, when and why.
sla_notes_daily_life: Article writing skills are useful for school magazines, blogs, journalism, research and community newsletters.
sla_exercise: What does a lead paragraph contain?::The main facts: who, what, where, when, why and how.||Name one feature of a journal article.::An abstract (or references, methods, discussion).||How does the tone of a magazine article differ from that of a journal article?::It is more engaging and informal than the formal academic tone of a journal.||What are the last steps in writing an article?::Editing and proofreading.

main_competence_name: Comprehend oral and written information
specific_competence_name: Comprehend oral messages with confidence and autonomy
learning_activity_name: Explain different types of meanings from oral information (e.g., denotative, connotative and figurative)
sla_name: Types of meaning in oral information
sla_assessment_criteria: Different types of meanings are clearly explained from oral information.
sla_teaching_aids: Recorded audio/video|Bluetooth speakers|IPA chart|Any relevant text
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Meaning in spoken language may be literal or implied depending on the speaker's intention and context.
sla_notes_details: Denotative meaning is the dictionary or literal meaning of a word. Connotative meaning is the emotional or cultural association attached to a word. Figurative meaning uses expressions such as metaphor, simile, idiom and hyperbole so that the meaning differs from the literal one. Learners listen to speeches, news items, songs and dialogues and identify the type of meaning used.
sla_notes_illustrations: The word home denotes a place where one lives, but connotes warmth and security. She has a heart of stone is figurative and means that she is unkind.
sla_notes_daily_life: Understanding these meanings prevents misunderstanding in conversations, advertisements and political speeches.
sla_exercise: Define denotation.::The literal or dictionary meaning of a word.||What is connotation?::The feelings or associations connected with a word.||What does the idiom to spill the beans mean?::To reveal a secret.||Name two figures of speech that give figurative meaning.::Metaphor and simile (or hyperbole, idiom).

main_competence_name: Comprehend oral and written information
specific_competence_name: Comprehend oral messages with confidence and autonomy
learning_activity_name: Explain meanings of oral texts derived from different registers (e.g., journalism, law, medicine and religion)
sla_name: Meanings of oral texts from different registers
sla_method: Scenario, Group discussions and Project work
sla_assessment_criteria: Meanings of texts from different registers are explained clearly.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A register is the variety of language used in a particular field or situation.
sla_notes_details: Learners listen to oral texts from journalism (news bulletins and interviews), law (court proceedings, oaths), medicine (consultations, health talks) and religion (sermons, prayers). They note specialised vocabulary (for example, plaintiff, adjourned, diagnosis, dosage, sermon), sentence structures and tone, and explain the meaning of the message in each field.
sla_notes_illustrations: In a court, the judge says: The case is adjourned until further notice, meaning that the hearing is postponed to a later date.
sla_notes_daily_life: Awareness of registers helps citizens understand court cases, doctors' instructions and news broadcasts.
sla_exercise: What is a register?::A variety of language used in a specific field or situation.||Give a word belonging to the legal register.::Plaintiff, defendant, verdict or adjourned.||Give a word belonging to the medical register.::Diagnosis, prescription or dosage.||What does adjourned mean in court?::Postponed to a later time.

main_competence_name: Comprehend oral and written information
specific_competence_name: Comprehend oral messages with confidence and autonomy
learning_activity_name: Describe rhetorical and implied meanings derived from conversations
sla_name: Rhetorical and implied meanings in conversations
sla_assessment_criteria: Rhetorical and implied meanings are correctly derived from conversations.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Implied meaning is what a speaker suggests without saying it directly, while rhetorical meaning is created by persuasive language.
sla_notes_details: Learners identify rhetorical questions (which need no answer), irony, understatement, sarcasm and hints. They use clues such as tone, stress, context and shared knowledge to infer implied meanings, and they discuss the speaker's purpose. Pragmatic notions such as implicature are introduced simply through examples.
sla_notes_illustrations: When a boss says: It is already ten o'clock, he may imply that the employee is late, even though he only states the time. The question: Who does not want peace? is rhetorical.
sla_notes_daily_life: Understanding implied meanings avoids misunderstanding in workplaces, negotiations and family conversations.
sla_exercise: What is a rhetorical question?::A question asked for effect that does not expect an answer.||What does the remark: Nice weather for a picnic! mean if said during a storm?::It is ironic, meaning the weather is bad.||Name two clues used to identify implied meaning.::Tone of voice and context.||What is sarcasm?::Saying the opposite of what one means in order to mock.

main_competence_name: Comprehend oral and written information
specific_competence_name: Comprehend oral messages with confidence and autonomy
learning_activity_name: Respond to oral messages with confidence and autonomy (e.g., seeking clarifications, adding comments, arguing and summarising)
sla_name: Responding to oral messages with confidence and autonomy
sla_assessment_criteria: Oral messages are responded to with confidence and autonomy.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Responding means reacting appropriately to what is heard, showing understanding and independent thinking.
sla_notes_details: Learners practise seeking clarification (Could you repeat that? What do you mean by...?), adding comments, arguing a position with reasons, and summarising the speaker's main points. They use active listening skills: focusing on the speaker, noting main ideas, avoiding interruptions and giving feedback with suitable body language and tone.
sla_notes_illustrations: After a talk on entrepreneurship a learner says: If I understand you correctly, you are saying that a business plan reduces risk. May I add that market research is equally important?
sla_notes_daily_life: Confident responses are needed in interviews, classroom discussions, meetings and customer service.
sla_exercise: Give two expressions used to seek clarification.::Could you repeat that? and What do you mean by...?||What is active listening?::Paying full attention, understanding and giving feedback to a speaker.||Why is summarising useful?::It confirms understanding and highlights the main points.||How can you disagree respectfully?::By acknowledging the point and giving a reasoned alternative view.

main_competence_name: Comprehend oral and written information
specific_competence_name: Construct complex and stylistic meanings from diverse and multiple texts
learning_activity_name: Use complex stylistic features (e.g., dialects, registers and figures of speech) obtained from written texts to convey meanings
sla_name: Complex stylistic features in written texts
sla_assessment_criteria: Complex stylistic features obtained from written texts are used correctly to convey messages.
sla_teaching_aids: Newspapers|Articles about environment|Gender|Drug abuse|HIV|Road safety|Human rights|Any other relevant texts
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Style is the way an author uses language to express ideas, and stylistic features are the devices that create it.
sla_notes_details: Learners identify dialects (regional or social varieties), registers, and figures of speech such as metaphor, simile, personification, irony, hyperbole, alliteration and symbolism, and discuss how they convey meaning, tone and mood. They also consider diction, sentence length and imagery, and explain how the writer's choices create effects.
sla_notes_illustrations: In the line: The wind whispered through the trees, personification gives the wind a human ability and creates a peaceful mood.
sla_notes_daily_life: Recognising style helps learners to analyse advertisements, speeches, poems and news commentaries critically.
sla_exercise: Define personification.::Giving human qualities to non-human things.||What is a dialect?::A variety of a language spoken by a particular region or social group.||Name two figures of speech.::Metaphor and simile (or hyperbole, irony).||What effect does a short sentence often create?::Emphasis or tension.

main_competence_name: Comprehend oral and written information
specific_competence_name: Construct complex and stylistic meanings from diverse and multiple texts
learning_activity_name: Explain meaning of written texts derived from different registers (journalism, medicine and religion)
sla_name: Meanings of written texts from different registers
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Written texts in different fields use particular vocabulary and structures, and the reader must interpret them correctly.
sla_notes_details: Learners read texts from journalism (news reports, editorials), medicine (leaflets, prescriptions and health articles) and religion (scriptural passages and devotional writing). They identify technical terms, sentence patterns, tone and purpose, and use context, dictionaries and background knowledge to explain the meaning of each text.
sla_notes_illustrations: A medicine leaflet says: Take two tablets twice daily after meals; the reader concludes that four tablets are taken a day in total.
sla_notes_daily_life: The skill helps people to follow medical instructions, understand news and interpret religious teachings.
sla_exercise: How many tablets in total are taken if the label says: Two tablets three times daily?::Six tablets.||What is the purpose of an editorial?::To give the newspaper's opinion on a current issue.||Name a feature of medical texts.::Technical terms such as dosage and symptoms.||Why is context important in understanding a specialised text?::It helps to identify the intended meaning of technical words.

main_competence_name: Communicate effectively in different contexts
specific_competence_name: Manage conversations with a good command of pronunciation
learning_activity_name: Interpret information from spontaneous and non-spontaneous conversations
sla_name: Interpreting information from conversations
sla_assessment_criteria: Information from spontaneous and non- spontaneous expressions are interpreted clearly.
sla_teaching_aids: Recorded audio/video|Bluetooth speakers|Any relevant text etc
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Interpreting information means understanding the message and intention in both planned and unplanned talk.
sla_notes_details: Spontaneous conversations are unplanned (casual talk, street conversation, phone calls) while non-spontaneous ones are planned (interviews, formal meetings, news broadcasts). Learners identify main ideas, details, attitude, topic shifts and the speaker's purpose, and note differences in structure, speed, hesitation and formality between the two types.
sla_notes_illustrations: In an interview the questions are prepared and answers are structured, while in a casual chat speakers use fillers such as well and you know and change topics freely.
sla_notes_daily_life: This skill helps in understanding lectures, interviews, meetings and everyday talk.
sla_exercise: Give an example of a spontaneous conversation.::A casual chat between friends.||Give an example of a non-spontaneous conversation.::A job interview or a formal meeting.||What are fillers?::Words like well, you know and er used while thinking.||Name one difference between formal and casual talk.::Formal talk is planned and polite; casual talk is relaxed with contractions.

main_competence_name: Communicate effectively in different contexts
specific_competence_name: Manage conversations with a good command of pronunciation
learning_activity_name: Apply pronunciation techniques in spontaneous and non-spontaneous conversations
sla_name: Pronunciation techniques in conversations
sla_method: Demonstration, Role- play and Follow-up interview
sla_assessment_criteria: Words and sentences are pronounced correctly using standard pronunciation, stress and intonation.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Pronunciation techniques are methods of producing English sounds and patterns so that speech is clear and easy to understand.
sla_notes_details: Techniques include correct articulation of sounds that are difficult for speakers of Bantu languages (such as the sounds in think and this, or the distinction between /l/ and /r/), word stress, sentence stress, intonation, rhythm, linking, and appropriate pace and volume. Learners use minimal pairs (ship and sheep), tongue twisters, recordings and dictionary transcriptions for practice.
sla_notes_illustrations: Minimal pairs such as light and right, or bit and beat, help learners to distinguish sounds and avoid misunderstanding.
sla_notes_daily_life: Good pronunciation builds confidence and helps workers such as tour guides, call-centre staff and teachers.
sla_exercise: What are minimal pairs? Give an example.::Words that differ by one sound, e.g. ship and sheep.||Name two techniques for improving pronunciation.::Practising tongue twisters and listening to recordings.||Why does stress matter?::It can change meaning and make speech understandable.||What is the difference between the vowels in bit and beat?::Bit has a short vowel /I/ and beat a long vowel /i:/.

main_competence_name: Communicate effectively in different contexts
specific_competence_name: Manage conversations with a good command of pronunciation
learning_activity_name: Participate in spontaneous and non-spontaneous conversations with people using different dialects of the English language
sla_name: Conversations with speakers of different English dialects
sla_assessment_criteria: Different dialects of English language are used correctly in spontaneous and non- spontaneous conversations.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: English has many dialects and accents, and effective speakers can communicate with people from different regions.
sla_notes_details: Learners study varieties such as British, American, Indian, Nigerian, Kenyan and Tanzanian English, noting differences in accent, vocabulary (lift and elevator, lorry and truck) and spelling (colour and color). Strategies for successful communication include listening for meaning, asking for repetition, speaking clearly, avoiding slang and showing respect for differences.
sla_notes_illustrations: A British speaker says lift, but an American says elevator; both refer to the same thing, and a good communicator understands both.
sla_notes_daily_life: This skill is needed in international meetings, tourism, online communication and studying abroad.
sla_exercise: Give one British and American vocabulary pair.::Lorry and truck (or lift and elevator).||What is an accent?::The way people pronounce a language.||Name a strategy for communicating with speakers of another dialect.::Asking for repetition or speaking clearly.||Why should we respect different dialects?::They are valid varieties of English that show cultural identity.

main_competence_name: Communicate effectively in different contexts
specific_competence_name: Create a variety of complex oral and written texts for different communicative purposes
learning_activity_name: Compare a variety of complex oral texts with appropriate prosodic features and correct grammar in different contexts.
sla_name: Comparing complex oral texts with prosodic features
sla_assessment_criteria: Various complex oral texts with appropriate prosodic features and correct grammar are compared well.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Prosodic features are the sound patterns of speech such as stress, intonation, rhythm, pitch and pace.
sla_notes_details: Learners listen to speeches, dialogues, news bulletins and poetry recitations and compare how prosody conveys attitude and emphasis. They also check grammar and appropriateness for the context, and contrast formal and informal texts in terms of pace, tone and structure.
sla_notes_illustrations: A news reader speaks slowly, with even pitch and clear pauses, while a football commentator uses a fast pace and rising pitch to show excitement.
sla_notes_daily_life: Comparing texts helps students to improve their own speaking for presentations and performances.
sla_exercise: Name two prosodic features.::Stress and intonation (or pitch, rhythm, pace).||How does a commentator's pace differ from that of a news reader?::It is faster and more excited.||What does a pause do in speech?::It separates ideas and gives emphasis.||What is pitch?::How high or low the voice sounds.

main_competence_name: Communicate effectively in different contexts
specific_competence_name: Create a variety of complex oral and written texts for different communicative purposes
learning_activity_name: Compose a variety of complex texts (e.g., investigative reports, academic reports, contracts, wills and complex instructional manuals) with appropriate punctuation and style
sla_name: Composing complex texts
sla_assessment_criteria: Variety of complex written texts are composed well with appropriate punctuations and style.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Complex texts are longer and more formal documents such as investigative reports, academic reports, contracts, wills and instructional manuals.
sla_notes_details: Each text has a fixed structure and register. An investigative report has a title, terms of reference, findings, conclusion and recommendations. A contract states the parties, obligations, payment, duration and signatures in precise legal wording. A will declares the testator, executor, beneficiaries and distribution of property. An instructional manual lists tools, steps in order, warnings and diagrams. Learners use accurate grammar, clear paragraphing and consistent tone.
sla_notes_illustrations: A manual for assembling a desk starts with: Requirements, then Step 1: Place the base on a flat surface, and includes a warning: Do not over-tighten the screws.
sla_notes_daily_life: These documents are used in business, law, education and technology.
sla_exercise: What are the main parts of an investigative report?::Title, findings, conclusion and recommendations.||What is a testator?::A person who makes a will.||Which tense mood is common in manuals?::The imperative.||Why must a contract be written precisely?::To avoid disputes about the agreed terms.

main_competence_name: Communicate effectively in different contexts
specific_competence_name: Create a variety of complex oral and written texts for different communicative purposes
learning_activity_name: Use prosodic features, punctuation and correct register to create a variety of complex oral and written texts for different communicative purposes
sla_name: Using prosodic features, punctuation and register in oral and written texts
sla_assessment_criteria: Prosodic features, punctuation and correct registers are correctly used to create complex oral and written texts.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Speakers use prosody to make meaning clear in speech, while writers use punctuation and register in writing.
sla_notes_details: Punctuation marks such as full stop, comma, semicolon, colon, dash, brackets and quotation marks correspond to pauses and tone in speech. Register must fit the purpose: formal for reports and applications, semi-formal for emails to colleagues and informal for messages to friends. Learners revise texts to correct punctuation and register mismatch.
sla_notes_illustrations: The sentence Lets eat, grandma may be changed by a comma into Let's eat, Grandma, which shows how punctuation changes meaning.
sla_notes_daily_life: Correct punctuation and register are important in emails, job applications and reports.
sla_exercise: What does a semicolon do?::It joins two closely related independent clauses.||Which register is used in a letter of application?::A formal register.||Punctuate: lets eat grandma.::Let's eat, Grandma.||Which spoken feature is equal to a comma in writing?::A short pause.

learning_activity_name: Differentiate intralingua, interlingua and sign language interpretations
sla_name: Differentiating intralingual, interlingual and sign language interpretation
sla_assessment_criteria: Intralingua, interlingua and sign language interpretations are differentiated correctly.
sla_teaching_aids: Recorded audio/ video of interpretation|Any other relevant materials
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Interpretation is the oral or signed conveying of a spoken message from one form into another in real time.
sla_notes_details: Intralingual interpretation is within the same language (for example, simplifying a legal speech in English into plain English). Interlingual interpretation is between two languages (for example, English to Kiswahili). Sign language interpretation renders spoken language into signs and vice versa for the deaf community. Modes include simultaneous, consecutive and whispered interpretation.
sla_notes_illustrations: During a presidential speech broadcast on television, a sign language interpreter stands beside the speaker and signs the message simultaneously.
sla_notes_daily_life: Interpreters are needed in courts, conferences, hospitals, schools for the deaf and international meetings.
sla_exercise: What is interlingual interpretation?::Interpretation between two different languages.||Name two modes of interpretation.::Simultaneous and consecutive.||Who benefits from sign language interpretation?::The deaf and hard-of-hearing community.||What is intralingual interpretation?::Interpretation within the same language.

main_competence_name: Provide advanced English language services to the community
specific_competence_name: Apply principles of interpretation to provide complex and authentic interpretations
learning_activity_name: Analyse theories and principles of interpretation
sla_name: Theories and principles of interpretation
sla_method: Read-Ink-Pair- Share (RIPS), Group discussion and Project work
sla_assessment_criteria: Theories and principles of interpretation are analysed clearly.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Theories of interpretation explain how meaning is understood and transferred from one speaker to another.
sla_notes_details: Learners study the interpretive theory of sense (understand, deverbalise, re-express), the effort model (listening, memory and production efforts) and the principles of accuracy, completeness, impartiality, confidentiality and clarity. They learn note-taking techniques for consecutive interpretation, use of symbols and abbreviations, and coping strategies for speed and terminology.
sla_notes_illustrations: In consecutive interpretation a speaker talks for two minutes, the interpreter uses symbols such as an arrow for cause or result and then delivers the message in the target language.
sla_notes_daily_life: These principles guide interpreters at conferences, in clinics and in courts.
sla_exercise: Name the three steps of the interpretive theory of sense.::Understanding, deverbalising and re-expressing.||Give two principles of interpretation.::Accuracy and confidentiality (or impartiality).||Why do interpreters use symbols in note-taking?::To record ideas quickly and accurately.||What is consecutive interpretation?::The interpreter speaks after the speaker has finished a segment.

main_competence_name: Provide advanced English language services to the community
specific_competence_name: Apply principles of interpretation to provide complex and authentic interpretations
learning_activity_name: Discuss the ethics of interpretation
sla_name: Ethics of interpretation
sla_assessment_criteria: Ethics of interpretation are well discussed.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Ethics are the moral standards that govern the conduct of interpreters.
sla_notes_details: The main ethical duties are confidentiality (not revealing information learned during work), impartiality (not taking sides), accuracy (not adding, omitting or changing), professional competence, respect for all parties, and honesty about limitations. An interpreter should declare conflict of interest and avoid giving personal opinions.
sla_notes_illustrations: If an interpreter in a hospital learns a patient's medical history, the ethics of confidentiality forbid discussing it with anyone else.
sla_notes_daily_life: Ethical interpreters earn trust in courts, hospitals and business talks.
sla_exercise: What is confidentiality?::Keeping information private.||Why should an interpreter be impartial?::To ensure fair communication for all parties.||What should an interpreter do if he has a conflict of interest?::Declare it and, if necessary, withdraw.||Name two other ethical duties.::Accuracy and professional competence.

learning_activity_name: Interpret conversations in a variety of settings
sla_name: Interpreting conversations in various settings
sla_assessment_criteria: Conversations in a variety of settings are interpreted correctly.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Settings for interpretation include community, business, educational and social situations.
sla_notes_details: Learners practise role plays of interpreting a conversation between English-speaking and Kiswahili-speaking people at a market, bank, school meeting or tourist site. They apply techniques of listening, memorising, note-taking and controlling turn-taking, and use first person (I) when interpreting for a speaker.
sla_notes_illustrations: A tourist asks: How much are these baskets? The interpreter tells the seller in Kiswahili: Vikapu hivi ni bei gani? and then conveys the response back in English.
sla_notes_daily_life: Interpreting skills help in tourism, community development and diplomacy.
sla_exercise: Which person should the interpreter use when speaking for someone?::The first person.||Give two settings in which interpretation is done.::Banks and hospitals (or markets, schools).||Why is turn-taking important?::It ensures each speaker is heard and interpreted clearly.||What skill helps recall long messages?::Note-taking and memory techniques.

learning_activity_name: Analyse theories and principles of translation
sla_name: Theories and principles of translation
sla_method: TIPS, Group discussion and project work
sla_assessment_criteria: Theories and principles of translation are analysed clearly.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Translation is the transfer of meaning from written text in one language to another.
sla_notes_details: Learners study equivalence theory (formal and dynamic equivalence), skopos theory (purpose of translation), and procedures such as literal translation, borrowing, calque, transposition, modulation and adaptation. Principles include fidelity to meaning, naturalness in the target language, consistency of terms and respect for culture.
sla_notes_illustrations: The English idiom It is raining cats and dogs is translated dynamically as Mvua kubwa inanyesha, not word for word.
sla_notes_daily_life: Translation is used in publishing, legal documents, subtitling, tourism materials and websites.
sla_exercise: Define translation.::Transferring the meaning of a written text from one language to another.||What is dynamic equivalence?::Translation that focuses on producing the same effect on the reader.||Name one translation procedure.::Borrowing (or calque, transposition, modulation).||Why is word-for-word translation sometimes wrong?::Idioms and structures differ between languages.

main_competence_name: Provide advanced English language services to the community
specific_competence_name: Apply principles of translation to produce complex authentic translation
learning_activity_name: Discuss the ethics of translation as a career
sla_name: Ethics of translation as a career
sla_assessment_criteria: Ethics of translation as a career are well discussed and appreciated.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Translation as a career has professional standards that protect clients and readers.
sla_notes_details: Ethical issues include confidentiality of documents, accuracy, avoiding plagiarism and copyright violation, honesty about skills and deadlines, fair pricing, impartiality and proper acknowledgement. Translators avoid machine-only output without human review and do not distort the source message for personal benefit.
sla_notes_illustrations: A translator of a company's financial report must not disclose the figures to competitors, because doing so would break confidentiality.
sla_notes_daily_life: Following ethics helps translators earn clients' trust and build a good reputation.
sla_exercise: Name two ethical duties of a translator.::Confidentiality and accuracy.||What is plagiarism?::Using another person's work without acknowledgement.||Why should translators meet deadlines?::It is part of professionalism and client trust.||What should a translator do when he does not know the subject?::Research or decline the job honestly.

learning_activity_name: Translate a variety of general texts using Computer-Assisted Translation (CAT) tools
sla_name: Translating general texts using Computer-Assisted Translation tools
sla_assessment_criteria: Variety of general texts are translated correctly using CAT tools.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Computer-Assisted Translation (CAT) tools are software applications that help human translators to work faster and more consistently.
sla_notes_details: CAT tools include translation memory (a database of previously translated segments), terminology databases or glossaries, alignment tools and quality checks. The translator opens a source document, the tool divides it into segments, suggests matches, and the translator accepts or edits them. CAT differs from machine translation, in which a computer produces the translation on its own.
sla_notes_illustrations: If the sentence Please submit your application was translated earlier, the translation memory suggests the same Kiswahili sentence when it reappears in a new document.
sla_notes_daily_life: CAT tools are used by translation agencies, software companies and international organisations.
sla_exercise: What is a translation memory?::A database that stores previous translations for reuse.||How does CAT differ from machine translation?::In CAT a human translator does the work with software support.||Name a benefit of using CAT tools.::Consistency and speed.||What is a glossary in translation?::A list of approved terms and their equivalents.

main_competence_name: Provide advanced English language services to the community
specific_competence_name: Apply principles of editing and proofreading a variety of texts
learning_activity_name: Analyse the theories and principles of editing and proofreading
sla_name: Theories and principles of editing and proofreading
sla_method: TIPS, Group discussion and Project work
sla_assessment_criteria: The theories and principles of editing and proofreading are analysed clearly.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Editing improves a text's content, structure and language, while proofreading is the final check for errors.
sla_notes_details: Levels of editing include developmental (content and organisation), substantive or copy editing (clarity, style, grammar and consistency) and proofreading (spelling, punctuation and formatting). Principles include respect for the author's voice, consistency, accuracy, fairness and use of style guides. Proofreading marks such as the caret (insert), delete sign and stet are used.
sla_notes_illustrations: An editor changes: The results was announced yesterday to The results were announced yesterday, and a proofreader corrects a misspelling like recieve to receive.
sla_notes_daily_life: Editing skills are used in publishing, journalism, offices and academic writing.
sla_exercise: What is the difference between editing and proofreading?::Editing improves content and style; proofreading checks final errors.||What does the mark stet mean?::Let it stand, ignore the correction.||Name one level of editing.::Copy editing (or developmental editing).||Correct: The informations are useful.::The information is useful.

main_competence_name: Provide advanced English language services to the community
specific_competence_name: Apply principles of editing and proofreading a variety of texts
learning_activity_name: Edit and proofread a variety of complex texts
sla_name: Editing and proofreading complex texts
sla_assessment_criteria: A variety of complex texts are edited and proofread correctly.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Complex texts such as reports, research papers and articles require careful editing and proofreading.
sla_notes_details: Learners read the whole text for sense, then check structure, paragraph unity, cohesion, style, tone and grammar. They correct spelling, punctuation, capitalization, tense consistency and repeated words, and check numbers, references and formatting. A checklist and a second reading of the text assist accuracy, and reading aloud or from the end helps to catch errors.
sla_notes_illustrations: In the sentence: Their going to present there findings tomorow, the editor corrects it to: They are going to present their findings tomorrow.
sla_notes_daily_life: This skill is used in preparing school magazines, official letters and dissertations.
sla_exercise: Correct: Their going to school.::They are going to school.||Why read a text aloud when proofreading?::It helps to detect errors and awkward phrases.||Give one item to check in formatting.::Spacing, headings or font consistency.||What is tense consistency?::Using the same tense throughout unless the time changes.

learning_activity_name: Assess the contribution of elements of form (e.g., plot, language and style) in shaping meanings of any literary work

sla_method: TIPS, Group discussion, Debate and Demonstration
sla_assessment_criteria: Contribution of elements of form in shaping meaning of any literary work is clearly examined.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Elements of form are the structural and stylistic components of a literary work, such as plot, language and style, that shape its meaning.
sla_notes_details: Plot arranges events to create suspense and meaning, language (diction, imagery and figures of speech) conveys feeling and theme, and style is the author's distinctive manner of writing. Learners study how the point of view, structure, setting and tone contribute to the message and judge how effectively the author uses them, supporting answers with quotations.
sla_notes_illustrations: In a novel narrated by a child, simple language and innocent tone highlight the cruelty of adult society and shape the reader's response.
sla_notes_daily_life: Analysing form helps readers to evaluate books, films and songs more critically.
sla_exercise: Name two elements of form.::Plot and style (or language, setting).||How does plot contribute to meaning?::It organises events to create suspense and develop themes.||What is style?::The author's distinctive way of using language.||Why should answers include quotations?::To provide evidence for the points made.

learning_activity_name: Relate the lesson from literary work to real life situations
sla_name: Relating lessons from literary works to real life

sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Literary works teach moral, social and political lessons that can be applied in real life.
sla_notes_details: Learners identify the message of a work (for example, honesty, hard work, resistance to oppression), examine the characters' choices and consequences, and connect them to issues in their communities such as corruption, gender inequality and poverty. Discussion and reflective essays help them to apply lessons in personal decision-making.
sla_notes_illustrations: A story in which a corrupt leader is finally punished teaches that dishonesty has consequences, and learners relate this to the real fight against corruption.
sla_notes_daily_life: Lessons from literature guide behaviour in families, schools and society.
sla_exercise: What is a moral lesson?::A message about right and wrong drawn from a story.||Give one social issue that literature often addresses.::Corruption (or gender inequality, poverty).||How can a student apply a lesson from a novel?::By making decisions guided by the values learned.||Why do writers include lessons in their works?::To teach, warn and inspire readers.

sla_name: Contribution of Tanzanian literature to a civilised society

sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Tanzanian literature reflects the history, culture and aspirations of the nation and helps to shape its values.
sla_notes_details: Learners study works by Tanzanian writers such as Shaaban Robert, Ebrahim Hussein, Penina Muhando, Abdulrazak Gurnah and Euphrase Kezilahabi. They examine how the works preserve culture, promote unity and language, criticise social evils, record history and motivate development, and how they contribute to civilisation through values of equality, justice and respect.
sla_notes_illustrations: A play that criticises exploitation of workers can raise public awareness and encourage fairness.
sla_notes_daily_life: Tanzanian literature strengthens national identity and is used in education, theatre and media.
sla_exercise: Name one Tanzanian writer.::Shaaban Robert (or Ebrahim Hussein, Abdulrazak Gurnah).||How does literature preserve culture?::By recording customs, values, language and history.||Give one role of literature in society.::Educating or criticising social evils.||What value does literature promote?::Unity, justice or respect.

sla_name: Distinctive features of literary genres
sla_assessment_criteria: Distinctive features of different genres of literature are clearly explained.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A genre is a category of literature with shared conventions, and the main genres are prose, drama and poetry.
sla_notes_details: Prose (novels and short stories) uses narration in paragraphs; drama is written to be performed, using dialogue, acts, scenes and stage directions; poetry uses verse, rhythm, rhyme, imagery and compression of language. Learners identify sub-genres such as tragedy, comedy, epic, ballad, elegy and satire and describe their features.
sla_notes_illustrations: A ballad is a narrative poem, often sung, that tells a story in short stanzas with a refrain.
sla_notes_daily_life: Knowing genres helps readers choose and appreciate the right type of book, play or song.
sla_exercise: Name the three main genres of literature.::Prose, drama and poetry.||What is a stanza?::A group of lines in a poem.||What is a tragedy?::A serious drama that ends in misfortune or death of the main character.||Which genre uses stage directions?::Drama.

sla_name: Applying theories of literature in critiquing works
sla_method: RIPS, Project work and Group work
sla_assessment_criteria: The theories of literature in critiquing literary works are correctly applied.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Literary theories are frameworks that guide how a work is interpreted and judged.
sla_notes_details: Learners apply theories such as formalism (focus on form and language), Marxism (class and economic relations), feminism (gender roles and power), post-colonialism (effects of colonial rule) and psychoanalysis (characters' minds). They read a chosen text, select a theory, gather evidence and write a critique that explains meaning and evaluates the work.
sla_notes_illustrations: A feminist reading of a novel about a woman denied education examines how patriarchal structures limit her opportunities.
sla_notes_daily_life: Critical thinking learned through theory helps in analysing media, politics and social issues.
sla_exercise: What does Marxist criticism focus on?::Class struggle and economic conditions.||What does feminist criticism examine?::Gender roles and power relations.||What is a critique?::A detailed critical evaluation.||Why apply a theory to a text?::To give a structured interpretation supported by evidence.

sla_name: Expressing a personal point of view after reading a literary work
sla_assessment_criteria: Personal point of view is expressed clearly.
sla_references: TET(2023), ENGLISH LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A personal response states what a reader thinks and feels about a work and gives reasons.
sla_notes_details: Learners state an opinion clearly, support it with evidence such as quotations and events, consider other interpretations, and use first person expressions (In my view, I believe). They discuss what they liked or disliked, whether the characters were convincing, and what the work taught them, in oral or written form.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student writes: In my view, the ending of the novel is effective because it leaves the reader thinking about the character's choice, as shown when she says: I cannot go back.
sla_notes_daily_life: Expressing opinions with evidence builds confidence and critical thinking for debates and reviews.
sla_exercise: Give an expression used to introduce an opinion.::In my view or I believe.||Why should opinions be supported by evidence?::To make them convincing and fair.||What is a book review?::A written evaluation of a book.||Should a reader consider other views? Why?::Yes, to be balanced and open-minded.
